top.line: How the Web Summit team works with agents: sessions, a conductor first, narrow roles, folders, keys.
top.para: An agent is a Claude Code session with a thread, files, a repository and a schedule. Everyone starts with a conductor, then one narrow role per session with a role file and a behaviour policy. Everything goes into the agent's folder so a new session can continue. Each agent publishes a public key by push, signs what it publishes and receives sealed secrets as QR codes. Humans give direction and pruning, and with seven people and a hundred agents, coordination is the work.

in-short.line: A session per agent, a conductor first, narrow roles, a folder, a key, and coordination.
in-short.para: Humans give the direction; agents are literal; the team is far past any team-size rule.

primitives.line: Claude reasons, GitHub holds the work, a session is an agent, and a schedule wakes it.
primitives.para: Scheduled tasks are a research preview with an hourly minimum; a session can also schedule messages back into itself. CLAUDE.md and role files are context, not rules: enforcement sits in the policy and the gate.

conductor.line: Everyone's first agent is a conductor, which reads, routes, schedules and reports.
conductor.para: Sign in at claude.ai/code, connect GitHub, choose the repository, say who you are, let it make its key and schedule, and correct its first plan. Screenshots are to come.

roles.line: One session per role, as narrow as possible, with a ROLE.md and a behaviour policy.
roles.para: Two kinds of developer, an adversarial analyst, the Sherpa and the advocate. Giving deployment to a different session is how a session avoids deploying by accident.

folders.line: Every person and every agent has a folder; the folder is the memory.
folders.para: A new session pointed at the folder continues where the last stopped; the team's conductor has had three sessions in five days. The per-person layout is the next step.

keys.line: Publishing the public key by push accepts an agent; signatures prove it holds the key.
keys.para: Secrets are sealed to the agent's key, handed over as QR codes, and signed by the sender, because a seal alone does not identify who sent it. pki.sgit.ai is our beta until the platform provides keys.

humans.line: Agents collaborate without politics but are literal and need direction and pruning.
humans.para: A security rule against outside scripts led a developer agent to copy everything across; a person had to say what the rule was for.

coordination.line: Brooks's law and two-pizza teams say this should not work; designed coordination is why it can.
coordination.para: n people have n(n-1)/2 paths; conductors, roles, folders, keys, briefs and policies are the coordination.

limits.line: Scheduled tasks are a preview, the layout a proposal, pki.sgit.ai a beta, screenshots to come.

sources.line: The memo, the Web Summit repository, Anthropic's docs, NIST, RFC 8032, AWS and Brooks.
